newsitem.title: USA: BBN sticks to FY97 view, cites Prop. 211.
newsitem.headline: BBN sticks to FY97 view, cites Prop. 211.

text.p: BBN Corp Chief Financial Officer Ralph Goldswasser reaffirmed the company aims to break even before interest, tax, depreciation and amortization (EBITDA) in the fiscal fourth quarter ending in June 1997.

But, citing next week's California vote on Proposition 211 which would make it easier to file class action shareholder lawsuits and make corporate officers individually liable, he and BBN Chief Executive George Conrades declined any fresh comment on future results.

"Although we have made foward-looking statements, which we stand by, we will not be making any additional forward-looking statements," Goldwasser said in a presentation to analysts here, noting 211 would increase exposure to shareholder suits.

Conrades had outlined the break-even EBITDA goal in remarks published in the BBN annual report. He also said in the report that BBN Planet's revenue is expected to increase 100 percent from fiscal year 1996 to fiscalyear 1997.
"While we expect substantial losses in fiscal year 1997, our goal is to return BBN to profitability by the end of fiscal year 1998," he wrote.

The two executives said that while the company continues to focus efforts on the Internet and on business and government customers, gross margins were currently in the five percent range during a period of investment.
Without making projections, they said an ideal model would produce 20 percent margins for the access segment of thebusiness, with margins doublethat for value-added services.
By the end of fiscal 1997, Conrades added, more than 50 percent of BBN's total revenues would be from services to the commercial sector.
